title: Directory Watcher Configuration Schema
description: JSON schema for the configuration file of Directory Watcher.

shell.description: Shell that runs every hook command. Defaults to sh on Unix and cmd on Windows. cmd and powershell (Windows PowerShell) are available only on Windows.

global.description: Global configurations applicable to all watch targets.

path.description: Path of the directory to monitor.

lifeCycle.description: Lifecycle hooks for this watch target.

onStartWatch.description: Commands to execute when starting to watch this directory.

onChange.description: Commands to execute when a change is detected in this directory.

onFinishWatch.description: Commands to execute when stopping watching this directory.

watch.description: What to watch: subfolders, excluded paths, and the file and folder events that run the hook.

exclude.description: Path patterns, relative to path, of files and folders to exclude from watching. Patterns are globs with ** and are checked in order; a pattern starting with ! watches a path excluded by an earlier pattern again. A matched folder and everything below it are not watched.

fileEvent.description: File events that run the hook (C: create or move in, U: update, D: delete or move away), or none. fileEvent and dirEvent cannot both be none.

dirEvent.description: Folder events that run the hook (C: create or move in, D: delete or move away), or none. A folder event stands for the folder and everything in it.

dirBatch.description: How events are collected into folder events.

waitMillisecond.description: Quiet time in milliseconds after the last event before collected folder events are sent. 0 turns collecting off.

maxWaitMillisecond.description: Longest time in milliseconds that folder events are collected. It cannot be less than waitMillisecond. If omitted, it is 1000, or waitMillisecond if that is larger.

hookBatch.description: How events are collected and merged into runs of the hook.

waitMillisecond.description: Quiet time in milliseconds after the last event before the collected events become runs. 0 does not wait: each event becomes runs on its own.

maxWaitMillisecond.description: Longest time in milliseconds that events are collected. It cannot be less than waitMillisecond. If omitted, it is 1000, or waitMillisecond if that is larger.

deliver.description: Runs made from the events collected in one wait. last: one run for the path that changed last, among the paths with a final change. lastPerPath: one run for each path with a final change, in the order the paths last changed. each: one run for each event, in the order the events happened.

queue.description: The queue of runs waiting for the hook.

size.description: Most runs that can wait in the queue. A run that does not fit stops the watcher with dispatch queue full. global.lifeCycle.onQueueWarning runs when the waiting runs reach 70% and 90% of size.

run.description: How runs of the hook are run.

concurrency.description: Most runs of the target that run at the same time. Runs start in the order their events happened and can end in any order.

interrupt.description: Running runs that a new run cancels before it starts. none: nothing; the new run waits for a free slot. samePath: the run of the same path, even when a slot is free. oldest: the run that started first, when every slot is taken; with concurrency 1, the running run.

onStartWatch.description: Commands to execute when starting the monitoring process.

onBeforeChange.description: Commands to execute before a change occurs.

onAfterChange.description: Commands to execute after a change occurs.

onError.description: Commands to notify once when the first fatal error wraps fsnotify.ErrEventOverflow. Error context is passed in DW_ERROR_* environment variables.

onQueueWarning.description: Commands to run when the runs waiting in a target's queue reach 70% or 90% of option.queue.size, or fall below 60% or 80% again. The warning is passed in DW_QUEUE_* environment variables.

onFinishWatch.description: Commands to execute when stopping the monitoring process.

anyOf.description: A command line run by the configured shell. Write template variables such as {{.Path}} outside quotes.
An object specifying the command and the directory in which to execute it.

dir.description: Directory path where the command will be executed.

anyOf.description: A command line run by the configured shell. Write template variables such as {{.Path}} outside quotes.
List of commands to execute sequentially.

cmd.description: Command or list of commands to execute.
